subject: general
question: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹3500 as a sum borrowed at 5% per year rate of interest for 2 years.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Effective Rate of Interest** for 2 years = Rate × Time = 5% × 2 = 10%.

**Simple Interest** = 10% of **Principal**.

SI = 10% of ₹3500 = (10/100) × 3500 = ₹350.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹350.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Principal (P)** = ₹3500

**Rate (R)** = 5% per annum

**Time (T)** = 2 years

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) / 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2a7b171d069779ecd644a54d8b028226f05476d28b26d5d468080095b632e6a8.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ SI = (3500 × 5 × 2) / 100

⇒ SI = (3500 × 10) / 100

⇒ SI = 35000 / 100

⇒ SI = ₹350

**∴ The correct answer is ₹350.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Amount Formula

The total amount (A) to be paid back is the sum of the principal and the simple interest: A = P + SI.

Direct Relation

Simple Interest is directly proportional to the principal, rate, and time. If any of these doubles (keeping others constant), the interest also doubles.

Compound Interest Difference

For a period of 2 years, the difference between Compound Interest (CI) and Simple Interest (SI) is given by: CI − SI = P(R/100)².
